title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes
journal: The New England Journal of Medicine

key_findings.claim: Semaglutide 2.4mg once weekly reduced composite cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke by 20% over 40 months
key_findings.citation_location: Lincoff et al., N Engl J Med 2023;389:2073-2084, Abstract Primary Outcomes
key_findings.clinical_interpretation: GLP-1 receptor agonism provides direct cardiovascular disease risk reduction beyond weight clearance alone.

key_findings.claim: Landmark trial enrolled 17,604 participants aged >=45 years with preexisting CV disease and BMI >=27 without diabetes
key_findings.citation_location: N Engl J Med 2023;389:2073-2084, Methods Trial Population
key_findings.clinical_interpretation: Cardiovascular protective benefits demonstrated in the largest GLP-1 cardiovascular outcomes study to date.

key_findings.claim: Primary CV endpoint event occurred in 6.5% on semaglutide vs 8.0% on placebo over 40 months follow-up
key_findings.citation_location: N Engl J Med 2023;389:2073-2084, Results Primary Cardiovascular Outcomes
key_findings.clinical_interpretation: Sustained long-term event reduction requires continuous physician monitoring rather than unguided intermittent use.
